source_snapshot.procedure: Enables ACS/AER, literal severity value 7EF6030 and SyncFlood settings, unlocks HDT, enumerates PCIe devices, then injects errortype 6 at hardcoded endpoint 0000:41:00.0 and root port 0000:40:01.1.
source_snapshot.criteria: Tool PASS and OS report within an undefined timeout; note identifies a Poisoned TLP at the root port or endpoint.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes only generic dmesg/rasdaemon capture, retains copied memory-function language and misstates the blast radius as memory-controller stress.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED; adds OCP topology and recovery gates but does not define the poison-consuming transaction, service/interface impact, severity-register decoding or distinct OCP coverage.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not prove the OCP target, Poisoned-TLP consumer, endpoint/root-port attribution or interface/service recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly gates operator injection and BDF validation but treats generic device health as sufficient without an OCP workload and dependency oracle.
historical_reviews.related_cases: PCIe companion row 57 has the same literal BDF pair; an OCP-labelled variant needs its own module identity, interface/service dependency and recovery evidence rather than duplicated PCIe wording.
historical_reviews.v3_1: OCP Poisoned-TLP acceptance requires physical-to-logical identity, isolated traffic, source/requester/completer attribution and deterministic non-fatal service recovery.

original_test_intent: Verify uncorrectable non-fatal Poisoned-TLP handling for every required OCP slot at both its endpoint and upstream root port, preserving the OCP link, interface and dependent service after the bounded error response.
original_method: Inventory each installed OCP module by physical slot, serial, firmware, driver, network or fabric interface and upstream PCIe path; identify management and production dependencies; decode AER severity/masks instead of trusting literal 7EF6030; baseline a disposable traffic flow; approve one harmless transaction that consumes poison; inject one endpoint or root-port source at a time; correlate exact AER source/status and traffic outcome; verify non-fatal containment plus link/interface/service recovery; restore all BIOS/HDT/AER state.
manual_activity: The FAE maps every physical OCP module through endpoint and root port, isolates management/production dependencies, approves the disposable poison-consuming traffic, executes one target at a time and owns interface, driver and platform recovery.
required_inputs: Physical OCP slot/module serial/firmware/driver/interface to endpoint and upstream root-port BDF map
Management, storage, fabric and production-service dependencies plus an independent OOB path
Disposable bounded traffic and exact transaction that safely consumes Poisoned TLP
AMD tool/spec version/hash/license and proof errortype 6 selects the intended endpoint/root source
Decoded 7EF6030 format/value with AER masks, DPC and SyncFlood policy
Expected AER source ID/status/severity, packet or I/O outcome, link/interface/service recovery, supported OS and timeout
safety_requirements: Dedicated quiesced OCP target with management access that does not traverse the tested interface
Re-enumerate module identity and upstream path immediately before injection; never reuse the companion PCIe BDFs
Use only disposable traffic and do not poison production, storage or cluster-control transactions
Inject one source only and abort on wrong AER source, fatal/DPC/SyncFlood escalation, driver reset outside plan, link loss or service impairment
No automatic retry; preserve evidence and restore/diff severity, AER, SyncFlood and HDT state
agent_execution_scope: Validate OCP identity/topology, dependency isolation, package semantics, severity policy and traffic oracle
Collect read-only PCIe/AER, link, driver, interface, traffic, service, OS/BMC and post-health evidence
Do not choose BDF/traffic, change BIOS/HDT, inject, reset/rebind/retry, touch production traffic or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve per-module endpoint/root-port target and isolated poison consumer
Supervise injection and OCP interface/service recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic dmesg and rasdaemon tails cannot attribute the OCP module, consuming transaction or service impact; memory-specific wording is unrelated.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Substitute live topology-verified OCP BDFs, run a bounded disposable traffic transaction, inject errortype 6 separately at endpoint or root port, and correlate precise AER source/status with link, interface and service recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The literal BDF examples, errortype 6, severity/SyncFlood settings, Poisoned-TLP note, OCP slot 1~N scope and 30/120-minute values remain preserved but gated.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run one topology-mapped OCP Poisoned-TLP injection against isolated disposable traffic and prove the intended non-fatal AER disposition plus link/interface/service recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds module identity, service dependencies, consumer traffic, source attribution, register decoding, an explicit non-fatal boundary and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tool PASS and generic OS log cannot prove Poisoned-TLP delivery, OCP slot coverage or preservation of network/fabric service.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Poison may abort packets or I/O, reset the device/driver, drop a management or fabric interface, trip DPC/SyncFlood or reset the host.

project_override_considerations: If an OCP module carries management, storage or cluster-control traffic and no independent recovery path exists, retain execution as pending. Do not treat the PCIe companion's hardcoded BDF pair as proof of this OCP path.
expected_evidence: Exact SUT and OCP module identity with physical slot, endpoint/root-port and dependency map
Tool/spec and decoded BIOS/AER severity/mask pre-state
Approved disposable traffic with baseline link/interface/service health
Separate target transcript with exact Poisoned-TLP AER source/status/severity
Traffic disposition and no fatal reset or persistent link/interface/service degradation
Restored state, post-health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: OCP slot 1~N is represented by the same single hardcoded BDF pair used by its PCIe companion and has no module, interface, service or distinct-coverage mapping. The source supplies no poison-consuming transaction or exact AER oracle; 7EF6030 is not decoded, timeout is undefined, RHEL 2022 is ambiguous and DeepSeek carries memory-specific language.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The OCP Poisoned-TLP UCE-nonfatal intent is identifiable. Engineering can supply module topology, dependency isolation, consumer traffic and oracle, so static review completes while execution remains gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 58 Wistron-System RAS-00778-V002: provide physical OCP slot/module/serial/FW/driver/interface-to-endpoint/root-port BDF and service-dependency mapping for slot 1~N, explain distinct coverage versus PCIe row 57, and define isolated traffic that safely consumes Poisoned TLP; approve AMD tool/spec and errortype=6 semantics, decode 7EF6030 plus masks/DPC/SyncFlood policy, and define exact AER source/severity plus link/interface/service recovery oracle, supported OS, timeout, aborts, OOB recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Separates OCP coverage from the companion PCIe case by requiring module identity, dependency-isolated consumer traffic and service recovery, preventing one copied BDF pair and generic log from standing in for every OCP slot.
independent_technical_reasoning: An OCP device may carry management, storage or fabric traffic, so a non-fatal AER label does not establish acceptable service impact. Poisoned-TLP behavior is testable only with a known consumer and attributable endpoint/root-port report. Because row 58 duplicates row 57 targets while changing only the item label, physical module and interface mapping is necessary to prove independent OCP coverage rather than a duplicate run.
